name: luh-datasets-for-classification-and-regression-in-human-robot-interaction-with-parallel-robots
notes:
This repository contains three datasets for the analysis of contact events in robots. The data was recorded using a parallel robot and is suitable for regression and classification tasks in the field of machine learning.

The datasets are divided into the following three tasks:

1.  **Regression of Contact Location and Force**: The goal is to predict the location and force of a contact on the robot.
2.  **Classification of the Collided Body**: This task aims to identify the robot's body that is in contact with the environment (one of the six links or the end-effector platform).
3.  **Classification of the Contact Type**: This task deals with distinguishing between different types of contact, such as collisions and clamping.

More details on the first two datasets can be found in the publication:
[https://doi.org/10.1109/IROS55552.2023.10342345](https://doi.org/10.1109/IROS55552.2023.10342345)

Information on the third dataset can be found here:
[https://doi.org/10.1109/IROS55552.2023.10341581](https://doi.org/10.1109/IROS55552.2023.10341581)

## Data Description

The data is available in `.csv` format and contains time-series data from the robot's sensors and a force-torque sensor. More information on the datasets can be found in their readme-files. The following variables are included in the datasets:

-   **`t_s`**: Time (s)
-   **`q_des_deg_[1-9]`**: Target joint angle for joints 1-9 (deg)
-   **`q_deg_[1-9]`**: Actual joint angle for joints 1-9 (deg)
-   **`x_des_m_rad_[1-3]`**: Target end-effector pose (x, y, orientation) (m, deg)
-   **`x_m_rad_[1-3]`**: Actual end-effector pose (x, y, orientation) (m, deg)
-   **`xd_ms_rads_[1-3]`**: Actual end-effector velocity (x, y, orientation) (m/s, deg/s)
-   **`tau_qa_Nm_[1-3]`**: Actual motor torque for motors 1-3 (Nm)
-   **`tau_ext_fts_Nm_[1-3]`**: External torque projected from force-torque sensor (Nm)
-   **`tau_ext_est_Nm_[1-3]`**: Estimated external torque (Nm)
-   **`F_ext_fts_N_Nm_[1-6]`**: External forces (1-3) and moments (4-6) from force-torque sensor (N, Nm)
-   **`F_ext_est_mobPlat_CS0_N_Nm_[1-3]`**: Estimated external force and moment on the mobile end-effector platform (N, Nm)
-   **`F_ext_fts_proj_mobPlat_CS0_N_Nm_[1-3]`**: Measured and projected external force and moment on the mobile end-effector platform (N, Nm)
-   **`distances_m_[1-3]`**: Distances for classification (m)
-   **`angles_deg_[1-3]`**: Angles for classification (deg)
-   **`collided_body`**: Identifier for the body in contact (1-6=links, 7=platform) (-)
-   **`chain`**: Collided chain (-)
-   **`link`**: Collided link of the chain (-)
-   **`location`**: Normalized location of the contact point on the link (-)
-   **`clamping_collision`**: Identifier for the type of contact (0=collision, 1=clamping) (-)

### Target Variables

-   **Regression**: `location` and the third component of `F_ext_fts_N_Nm_[1-6]` (link-orthogonal force).
-   **Classification of the Collided Body**: `collided_body`.
-   **Classification of the Contact Type**: `clamping_collision`.

## Usage

The datasets are available as `train.csv` and `test.csv` (for the classification tasks) and `data.csv` (for the regression task). They can be loaded using common libraries like Pandas in Python to train and evaluate machine learning models.

## Citation

If you use these datasets in your research, please cite the corresponding publications.
title: Datasets for classification and regression in human-robot interaction with parallel robots

# Classification of Collided-Body Classification

This project deals with the collided-body classification. The goal is to determine the collided body of a parallel robot which can be one of its six links or the end-effector platform. More information can be found in the publication [https://doi.org/10.1109/IROS55552.2023.10342345](10.1109/IROS55552.2023.10342345)

## Project Structure

The project directory contains the following files:

-   `main.py`: The main Python script. It loads the training and test data and visualizes the data by generating three distinct 3D scatter plots for EE pose, distances and angles.
-   `train.csv`: The training dataset. Contains time-series data from the robot, including joint angles, end-effector coordinates, forces, and torques. This data is used to train a classification model.
-   `test.csv`: The test dataset. It has the same structure as `train.csv` and is used to evaluate the performance of the trained model.


## Data Description

The `.csv` files contain the following variables:

-   **`t_s`**: Time (s)
-   **`q_des_deg_[1-9]`**: Target joint angle for joints 1-9 (deg)
-   **`q_deg_[1-9]`**: Actual joint angle for joints 1-9 (deg)
-   **`x_des_m_rad_[1-3]`**: Target end-effector pose (x, y, orientation) (m, deg)
-   **`x_m_rad_[1-3]`**: Actual end-effector position (x, y, orientation) (m, deg)
-   **`tau_qa_Nm_[1-3]`**: Actual motor torque for motors 1-3 (Nm)
-   **`tau_ext_fts_Nm_[1-3]`**: External torque projected from force-torque sensor (Nm)
-   **`tau_ext_est_Nm_[1-3]`**: Estimated external torque (Nm)
-   **`F_ext_fts_N_Nm_[1-6]`**: External forces (1-3) and moments (4-6) from sensor. The third component represents the link-orthogonal force. (N, Nm)
-   **`F_ext_fts_proj_mobPlat_CS0_N_Nm_[1-3]`**: Measured and projected external force and moment on the mobile end-effector platform in base frame (N, Nm)
-   **`F_ext_est_mobPlat_CS0_N_Nm_[1-3]`**: Estimated external force and moment on the mobile end-effector platform in base frame (N, Nm)
-   **`distances_m_[1-3]`**: Distances for classification (m)
-   **`angles_deg_[1-3]`**: Angles for classification (deg)
-   **`collided_body`**: Identifier for the body in contact (1-6=links, 7=platform) (-)

## Execution

To run the main script and display the visualization, ensure you have Python and the following libraries installed:

-   pandas
-   numpy
-   matplotlib

You can install the required libraries using pip:

```bash
pip install pandas numpy matplotlib
```

Then, run the script from your terminal:

```bash
python main.py
```

The script will load the data and display three 3D plots.

# Classification of Contact-Type

## Project Structure

The project directory contains the following files:

-   `main.py`: The main Python script. It loads the training and test data and visualizes the data by generating three distinct 3D scatter plots for end-effector pose, distances and estimated external forces.
-   `train.csv`: The training dataset. Contains time-series data from the robot, including joint angles, end-effector coordinates, forces, and torques. This data can used to train a classification model.
-   `test.csv`: The test dataset. It has the same structure as `train.csv` and is used to evaluate the performance of the trained model.

# Regression of Location and Force

This project deals with the regression of contact location and forces. More information can be found in the publication [https://doi.org/10.1109/IROS55552.2023.10342345](10.1109/IROS55552.2023.10342345)

## Project Structure

The project directory contains the following files:

-   `main.py`: The main Python script. It loads the data and visualizes the data by generating a 2D scatter plot for contact location and forces.
-   `data.csv`: The dataset. Contains time-series data from the robot, including joint angles, end-effector coordinates, forces, and torques. This data can used to train a regression model.


## Data Description

The `.csv` files contain the following variables:

-   **`t_s`**: Time (s)
-   **`q_des_deg_[1-9]`**: Target joint angle for joints 1-9 (deg)
-   **`q_deg_[1-9]`**: Actual joint angle for joints 1-9 (deg)
-   **`x_des_m_rad_[1-3]`**: Target end-effector pose (x, y, orientation) (m, deg)
-   **`x_m_rad_[1-3]`**: Actual end-effector pose (x, y, orientation) (m, deg)
-   **`xd_ms_rads_[1-3]`**: Actual end-effector velocity (x, y, orientation) (m/s, deg/s)
-   **`tau_qa_Nm_[1-3]`**: Actual motor torque for motors 1-3 (Nm)
-   **`F_ext_fts_N_Nm_[1-6]`**: External forces (1-3) and moments (4-6) from sensor. The third component represents the link-orthogonal force. (N, Nm)
-   **`F_ext_est_mobPlat_CS0_N_Nm_[1-3]`**: Estimated external force and moment on the mobile end-effector platform in base frame (N, Nm)
-   **`F_ext_fts_proj_mobPlat_CS0_N_Nm_[1-3]`**: Measured and projected external force and moment on the mobile end-effector platform in base frame (N, Nm)
-   **`collided_body`**: Identifier for the body in contact (1-6=links, 7=platform) (-)
-   **`chain`**: Kinematic chain of the collided body (-)
-   **`link`**: Link of the collided body in the kinematic chain (-)
-   **`location`**: Normalized location of the contact point on the link (-)

## Execution

To run the main script and display the visualization, ensure you have Python and the following libraries installed:

-   pandas
-   numpy
-   matplotlib

You can install the required libraries using pip:

```bash
pip install pandas numpy matplotlib
```

Then, run the script from your terminal:

```bash
python main.py
```

The script will load the data and display a 2D plot.
